subject: Install Help for STAN and rstan

messages.author: 7dd668eb41c5bfd9
messages.subject: Install Help for STAN and rstan
parts:
Hi,

This might seem like a simple question, but I'm having trouble installing STAN and RStan on my Mac.

For STAN, I followed the directions in the reference manual. I downloaded the source code, unpacked it to a folder in my Applications directory. I've verified that I have the neccessary versions of make and g++. When I navigate to my stan folder, I run

make bin/libstan.a

and I get the error:

make/tests:169: *** multiple target patterns.  Stop.

I've  tried looking this up, but I couldn't find anything.

Second, when I try to install RStan, I followed the directions on the website. I installed Rcpp and inline packages. I verified that I have a C++ compiler (the 'hello world' code worked). But when I try to install RStan, I get the error 

ERROR: failed to lock directory ‘/Users/Nate/Library/R/3.0/library’ for modifying
Try removing ‘/Users/Nate/Library/R/3.0/library/00LOCK-rstan’

There is no folder called 00LOCK-rstan in my directory and if I run 

remove.packages('rstan')

I get an error that there is no package called rstan installed.

What am I doing wrong?

Thanks,

Nate

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Install Help for STAN and rstan
parts:
On 11/4/13, 3:56 PM, Nathan Lemoine wrote:
> Hi,
>
> This might seem like a simple question, but I'm having trouble installing STAN and RStan on my Mac.

Just a heads up: you don't need command-line Stan in order to run RStan.

You'll need to give us a little more info before
we can help you debug. Which version of Mac OS are
you using and which version of g++ and make (you can type
"g++ -v" and "make -v" in a shell for the latter)?
> For STAN, I followed the directions in the reference manual. I downloaded the source code,

From a GitHub branch or one of our stable distributions? If
the latter, which one? If the former, when?

> unpacked it to a folder in my
> Applications directory. I've verified that I have the neccessary versions of make and g++. When I navigate to my stan
> folder,

You should be able to run "ls" and see the top-level makefile
and src directory if you're in the right location.

I run
>
> make bin/libstan.a
>
> and I get the error:
>
> make/tests:169: *** multiple target patterns. Stop.
>
> I've tried looking this up, but I couldn't find anything.

Basically, all the online info I found just repeats the message.

Have you perhaps modified the makefile? I'd try downloading
it again or unpacking from the tarball you have depending on
how you downloaded it. You shouldn't get this problem if you
don't have a corrupted makefile.

> Second, when I try to install RStan, I followed the directions on the website. I installed Rcpp and inline packages. I
> verified that I have a C++ compiler (the 'hello world' code worked). But when I try to install RStan, I get the error
>

> ERROR: failed to lock directory ï¿½/Users/Nate/Library/R/3.0/libraryï¿½ for modifying
> Try removing ï¿½/Users/Nate/Library/R/3.0/library/00LOCK-rstanï¿½

I'm not an R expert, but can you search for a file 00LOCK-rstan using
Spotlight and see if you have one anywhere? I don't know what R uses
them for, but files with "LOCK" in the name are typically used for
old-school process-level synchronization. If something dies in the middle
without cleaning up the lock, you basically have problems because you
can't start a process again if there's already a lock file that it's
expecting to create in place.

> There is no folder called 00LOCK-rstan in my directory and if I run
>
> remove.packages('rstan')
>
> I get an error that there is no package called rstan installed.

Right -- you bombed out in the middel of the install. You may need
to find where it partially installed and just clean everything out.

R users tend to just reinstall R from scratch when something like
this goes wrong! But you can probably affect a subtler fix by just
cleaning out the litter from the failed install and trying again.

Make sure you follow the instructions to shut down and restart R
in between installs.
> What am I doing wrong?

Hard to know without more info. I wish we could make this process
easier for users, but R is super stateful, and it can get itself
into a knot like you've found that you can't get out of from within
R itself.

- Bob

Thanks for the response. I have looked for the 00LOCK file in spotlight and in hidden files and found nothing.

I did get rstan installed successfully. The issue was, I think, actually really simple. I was running two R consoles, and I had tried to install rstan on one of them. I shut them both down and restarted and it installed fine. It looks like there was an issue with running two consoles at once.

this problem can creep in through template matching if
the path contains a colon (I didn't even know that was
legal in a file name). For instance, it seems a common problem
on Cygwin for Windows when using absolute Windows path names with
colons in them.

Nathan,

I have a guess as to what's going on. I'll start with a possible workaround:
  • Try replacing your make/tests with the one attached. It just has lines 131 to 145 commented out.
Please let us know if that works. Sorry about the difficulties -- our builds definitely shouldn't fail in this way.


What I think is happening:
There's a call to Rscript in make/tests used to shuffle tests. My guess is that in your configuration of R, there are some libraries that are automatically loaded. We use that output to generate dependencies: if that has a colon in it, make won't be able to handle it.

Would you mind running this line from the terminal and letting us know the output?
Rscript -e "cat(sample(commandArgs(trailingOnly=TRUE)))" 1 2 3

If that is the cause of the problem, I'll create an issue for it and get it patched asap. I'm moving the technical discussion to the stan-dev mailing list.



Daniel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Install Help for STAN and rstan
parts:
For what it's worth, I suspect this problem hasn't come up much because most people with custom R profiles are heavy R users and probably installed Rstan (which works fine for me).

The only reason I even found out this was a problem was because I didn't understand that Rstan was completely self-contained. I thought it was similar to Rjags, where I needed a base install of Stan that Rstan calls from R. If I had known what I was doing, I probably wouldn't have bothered with the command line version and never would have encountered the problem.

On Nov 6, 2013, at 3:27 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

You can also work around it using the answer I gave here:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/16990833/error-instaling-rstan-on-rstudio-server

Ben

Yes, thank you for reporting back. It confirms what I thought was the cause of the issue.

Sorry again for the installation trouble. These are definitely on our build side and we'll try to get it worked out asap.


Daniel
